ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The attached diagram shows a 5 by 5 box divided into unit cells. Reading rows from top to bottom and columns from left to right, the seven 1 by 3 bars occupy these positions: a vertical bar in column 1, rows 1-3; a horizontal bar in row 1, columns 2-4; a horizontal bar in row 2, columns 2-4; a vertical bar in column 2, rows 3-5; a vertical bar in column 5, rows 1-3; a horizontal bar in row 4, columns 3-5; and a horizontal bar in row 5, columns 3-5. Thus the empty cells visible in the diagram are column 1 rows 4-5 and row 3 columns 3-4. Reasoning: A new 1 by 3 bar needs three consecutive empty unit cells in a row or column. Initially the four empty cells do not contain any straight run of length 3, so zero moves is impossible. Initially, the only bar that can start sliding is the left vertical bar in column 1, because it has empty cells directly below it; all other bars are blocked at their sliding ends. Slide this left vertical bar down two cells so it occupies column 1, rows 3-5. Then column 1, rows 1-2 become empty, while row 3 columns 3-4 remain empty. This allows the two upper horizontal bars, in rows 1 and 2, to slide left one cell each. If only one of those two upper bars is moved, there is still no straight run of three empty cells, so using only two moved bars total cannot be enough. But with three moved bars, slide the left vertical bar down two cells, slide the row-1 horizontal bar left one cell, and slide the row-2 horizontal bar left one cell. These moves vacate column 4 in rows 1, 2, and 3, giving three consecutive empty cells for a new vertical 1 by 3 bar. Therefore the minimum number of bars that must be moved is 3.

Check that initially no three consecutive empty cells exist, and the only bar that can start moving is the left vertical bar, sliding down into the two empty cells below it. After moving that bar down to column 1 rows 3-5, the empty cells in column 1 rows 1-2 allow the two upper horizontal bars to slide left. This vacates column 4 rows 1-3, giving room for one new vertical 1 by 3 bar. Therefore the minimum is 3.

Slide this left vertical bar down two cells so it occupies column 1, rows 3-5. Then column 1, rows 1-2 become empty, while row 3 columns 3-4 remain empty. This allows the two upper horizontal bars, in rows 1 and 2, to slide left one cell each. If only one of those two upper bars is moved, there is still no straight run of three empty cells, so using only two moved bars total cannot be enough. But with three moved bars, slide the left vertical bar down two cells, slide the row-1 horizontal bar left one cell, and slide the row-2 horizontal bar left one cell. These moves vacate column 4 in rows 1, 2, and 3, giving three consecutive empty cells for a new vertical 1 by 3 bar. Therefore the minimum number of bars that must be moved is 3.
